fieldNotes.location: 243 Urban St, Buffalo NY. ROOFTOP geocode confirmed (moved 99m). Building positively identified: large multi-section/multi-story historic brick manufacturing complex on Buffalo's East Side, pink grain-silo tower landmark, rail line on the east side. Web-confirmed as the J.M. Smucker Milk-Bone plant (550,000 sq ft, dog-treat ops since 1925, $53M renovation underway, completion April 2027).
fieldNotes.truckGate: TWO controlled truck entrances. (1) The dedicated drop yard NW of the plant has a wide chain-link SLIDING GATE across its truck driveway (Street View 2025-07 from Urban St shows the slider clearly). (2) The fenced truck/dock yard at the building has sliding chain-link gates. truckGateCount set to 2.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed guard booth observed at either truck gate in Street View 2025-07 or satellite z20-z21. A small structure sits at the SW corner of the building yard but is not positioned/shaped as an entry guard booth (more a utility/scale-house type). Treated as unmanned controlled gates. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: True - controlled gates exist but no guard booth, implying kiosk/app/call-box check-in.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Large dedicated trailer-storage lot NW of the plant building (mostly gravel, with an internal paved loop drive), packed with rows of parked drop trailers. Separate from active dock staging.
fieldNotes.dropArea: 50+ - trailer rows in the drop yard count well above 50 stalls' worth of trailers.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: ~14 dock doors estimated across the building's E/SE faces; the multi-story masonry plant makes door counting harder than a modern tilt-up - flagged uncertain. Band 10-25.
fieldNotes.railServed: A CSX/active rail line runs immediately along the east property edge with rail cars present, but no rail spur was observed entering the property to a building face. Set false (rail-adjacent, not rail-served).
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: The drop yard has a wide gravel apron and ample unused paved/graded width at the gate - room to add a bypass/express lane.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: The drop yard interior holds a deep queue (3+ trucks) between the sliding gate and the trailer rows.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Dense East Side Buffalo urban fabric - row houses on all surrounding streets. Urban.
fieldNotes.yardMetrics: trailersVisible ~48 and trailerParkingCapacity ~70 are honest estimates from z19 imagery; dock count low-confidence.

citations.claim: Smucker sold value pet brands to Post but RETAINED Milk-Bone and Meow Mix.
Milk-Bone plant at 243 Urban St Buffalo operating under Smucker (~280 employees); $52M Smucker expansion.

verification.rationale: Milk-Bone retained in the 2023 Post divestiture; Buffalo plant active with a 2025 $52M Smucker expansion.
